simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to חֵדֶק (H2312) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: חֵדֶק (chêdeq) means a prickly plant First listed occurrence: Mic 7 4.

definitions.full: H2312. chedeq חֵ֑דֶק noun [masculine] brier (Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic חִדְקָא Löw p. 147, No. 104 ; compare Arabic a kind of night-shade, see Lane 532 ); — כַּחֵדֶק טוֺבָם Micah 7:4 the best of them (si vera lectio) is like the brier (|| מִמְּסוּכָה יָשָׁר ); חָ֑דֶק כִּמְשֻׂכַת עָצֵל דֶּרֶךְ Prov 15:19 the way of a sluggard is like a brier-hedge.
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to sting;
